subject: Follow-up: Reliability & SLOs — Redwood vs Hyperscalers
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecloud.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Reliability & SLOs — Redwood vs Hyperscalers

Thanks for the call earlier today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (what we covered)
- High-level: AcmeCloud is evaluating inference providers for production traffic (latency-sensitive customer-facing features). You wanted a clear comparison vs hyperscalers on uptime, rate limits, error budgets, and failover behavior.
- Redwood differentiators we emphasized: production-first runtime, configurable rate-limit tiers, prefix/KV caching to reduce tail latency, multi-region active-passive failover with warm standby, and observable error budgets tied to routes.

SLO / Reliability baseline (Redwood vs typical hyperscaler patterns)
- Uptime SLA: Redwood (99.95% platform SLA for Dedicated / Enterprise customers) vs many hyperscaler-managed endpoints commonly advertised at 99.9% for multi-tenant endpoints.
- Rate limits & concurrency: Redwood configurable per-customer rate tiers; we can support sustained per-tenant throughput >500 rps in Dedicated with burst to 2k rps depending on instance commit. Public hyperscaler endpoints often impose stricter per-key qps and automatic throttling that reduces sustained concurrency.
- Error budgets: We provide route-level error budget tracking with alerts and automatic fallback routing to a lower-capacity replica model if thresholds are exceeded. Hyperscalers typically expose global metrics but less granular route-level automated fallback.
- Failover behavior: Redwood supports cross-region failover with warm KV cache priming to minimize cold-KV penalties. Failover is policy-driven (can be automatic or manual) and we provide documented RTO/RPO targets per deployment.

Proposed next tests (so you can validate claims)
1) Functional smoke: end-to-end inference on a sample customer prompt set (validate deterministic outputs / prompt handling).
2) Load test: sustained 1k rps for 30 minutes from your traffic generator (P95 latency target < 250ms on Dedicated plan; we’ll run from us-west region).
3) Failover injection: simulate primary region outage and validate automatic failover and recovery behavior, capture cold-KV latency spike and warm-up timeline.
4) Rate-limit exercise: constrained quota test to observe degradation/fallback semantics and error codes returned.

Attachments: I attached an SLO comparison spreadsheet and a mutual action plan (MAP) with proposed responsibilities and timeline.

Next steps
- Ben/Aditya run the initial smoke test on Thurs 2026-03-05 10:00 PT if that works for your team.
- Samantha/Tom confirm the traffic generator details and whether you want Redwood to run the load or if you’ll run it from your side.

Thanks — we’ll prepare a runbook and a short playbook for failover steps.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0147

--

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reliability & SLOs — Redwood vs Hyperscalers

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs before we lock the test window: 

1) Rate limits — when you say "configurable per-customer rate tiers," can you confirm the default per-API-key soft limit for hosted (non-dedicated) vs what you guarantee on Dedicated? We need to understand throttling behavior for hero customers.
2) Failover — is the cross-region failover automatic by default for Dedicated, or do we need to enable it? In the past with other providers we saw long cold-cache penalties; can you quantify typical cold-KV penalty and how long warm-priming takes?
3) SLA & credits — our procurement will want exact language on 99.95% SLA and credits. Do you have a sample SOW or SLA doc?
4) SOC2 evidence — we need a point of contact for security/compliance docs and the expected lead time to provide SOC2 artifacts.

Prefer Redwood to run the first load test (so we can pair on monitoring). If you can run it Thurs 3/5 at 10am PT that works for our infra folks — Tom will join.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director of Product Ops | AcmeCloud
Samantha.Lee@acmecloud.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecloud.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 21:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Reliability & SLOs — Redwood vs Hyperscalers

Hey Samantha — quick answers and links below; happy to expand on the call.

1) Rate limits
- Hosted (multi-tenant): default soft limits are 60 qps per API key with per-minute burst protection; this is intended for onboarding and low-volume apps.
- Dedicated/Enterprise: we provision per-tenant capacity based on committed units. Typical reserved capacity for Dedicated starts at the 500 rps sustained band; we can set higher reserved throughput with instance commits. We also expose a per-route concurrency override to protect tail latency for critical routes.
- If you want, for the load test we’ll provision a Dedicated test pool (no production traffic mixed in) so you see true behavior.

2) Failover / cold-KV penalty
- Failover is optional; for Dedicated customers it’s enabled via configuration (we can set automatic failover for this POC).
- Cold-KV penalty: on a full cold start (no prefix/KV warm), median added latency is ~120-200ms for large models we typically serve; with warm-priming we can bring that down to single-digit ms for cached prefixes. During our failover test we’ll measure cold vs warm.

3) SLA & credits
- We have a standard SLA doc for Dedicated customers (99.95% monthly uptime). I linked the SLA and SOW templates here: https://docs.redwood.ai/slo-and-reliability#sla-template. Procurement: we can provide redlines but the SLA language in that doc is the baseline.

4) SOC2 / compliance
- Point of contact: me (aditya_rao@redwood.ai) for initial requests; our security team usually responds within 3 business days with a secure download link for SOC2 artifacts and evidence. For deeper audits we coordinate an evidence timeline in the MAP.

Runbook & test logistics
- Drive link with the runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/AcmeCloud/SLO-matrix (attached in Ben’s email).
- For Thurs 3/5 10:00 PT we’ll: provision a Dedicated test pool, run a 10-min smoke, then the sustained 30-min 1k rps test, then the failover injection. We’ll stream logs/traces to your SRE Slack channel (please confirm invite).

I’ll also attach the SLO matrix and a short runbook to the HubSpot deal.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
